paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. When God speaks, His word does not fail. Jehu tells the people, "Know, then, that not a word the LORD has spoken against the house of Ahab will fail, for the LORD has done what He promised through His servant Elijah." (2 Kings 10:10). Seventy sons, a fortified city, chariots, horses, weapons, and none of it stood in the way.

I think this is a heavy one, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Jehu says "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD!" (2 Kings 10:16), but notice that the zeal is Jehu's own claim. The text lets his word stand there, and it doesn't hand him a gold star for it. So the baker can hold two things at once: God's word comes true, and a man saying he's zealous for the LORD is not the same as the LORD saying so.

So here's what I'd take to the oven, friend. Read what God has said, and trust it more than any loud voice, even a loud voice with a chariot. Whatever's standing between you and His word, it will not outlast it. And this story isn't over, because Jehu's chariot is still rolling.
